title: Progress towards measles and rubella elimination in Lesotho, 2011–2025
abstract: BACKGROUND: Lesotho, a lower middle-income country in southern Africa, has historically had relatively high routine immunization coverage over the last three decades. Since 1996, the country has been implementing measles elimination strategies. This manuscript evaluates Lesotho's performance, from 2011 to 2025, against the World Health Organization's criteria for measles and rubella elimination. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective review of Lesotho's immunization and surveillance data during 2011-2025. This included Lesotho's annual WHO/UNICEF Estimates of National Immunization Coverage (WUENIC) for routine measles-containing vaccine (MCV) doses; performance in the periodic measles rubella vaccination campaigns and case-based surveillance; and the trends of measles and rubella incidences. RESULTS: During 2011-2025, MCV1 coverage generally remained ≥90% but failed to reach the 95% elimination target. MCV2 coverage reached 80% in 2011 and 2012 before declining in subsequent years. Lesotho has mostly attained the targets for surveillance performance according to the two principal performance indicators - non-measles febrile rash illness rate and the proportion of districts that report a minimum of one suspected case. From 2011 to 2015, measles incidence stayed below one per 1 million population in Lesotho. However rubella incidence ranged between 33.4 in 2012 to 142.3 in 2014, and declined significantly after MR introduction in 2017. CONCLUSION: Lesotho has made significant progress in measles and rubella elimination efforts. To sustain the gains made, the country should work to strengthen vaccination in the second year of life, reinforce demand generation during preventive campaigns, address population denominator inaccuracies that hinder accurate coverage tracking, and systematically document measles and rubella virus genotypes.

To sustain the gains made, the country should work to strengthen vaccination in the second year of life, reinforce demand generation during preventive campaigns, address population denominator inaccuracies that hinder accurate coverage tracking, and systematically document measles and rubella virus genotypes.

title: Deterministic and ANN-based modelling of measles transmission using real epidemiological data
abstract: This study aims to develop a nonlinear SVLIQR epidemic model to investigate measles transmission dynamics by incorporating vaccination, latency, quarantine, and treatment effects. The qualitative properties of the model, including positivity and boundedness of solutions, are established. The basic reproduction number is derived using the next-generation matrix method, and the existence of disease-free and endemic equilibrium points is examined. The local stability of the disease-free equilibrium is analysed using the Routh-Hurwitz criterion, while global stability is studied through the Castillo-Chávez approach. In addition, model parameters are estimated using the least squares method based on reported measles cases in China from 2005 to 2017. To improve the numerical approximation and capture the nonlinear dynamics of the system, an ANN-based solver coupled with the ode45 scheme is implemented. The results show that the model fits the reported data well, and the ANN framework provides highly accurate and convergent approximations under different epidemiological parameter settings. Numerical simulations further indicate that higher vaccination and quarantine rates significantly reduce measles transmission. Overall, the proposed framework provides a useful and reliable tool for understanding measles dynamics and assessing effective intervention strategies.

title_zh: 基于确定性和人工神经网络的麻疹 传播动力学建模研究
source_body_en: This study aims to develop a nonlinear SVLIQR epidemic model to investigate measles transmission dynamics by incorporating vaccination, latency, quarantine, and treatment effects. The qualitative properties of the model, including positivity and boundedness of solutions, are established. The basic reproduction number is derived using the next-generation matrix method, and the existence of disease-free and endemic equilibrium points is examined. The local stability of the disease-free equilibrium is analysed using the Routh-Hurwitz criterion, while global stability is studied through the Castillo-Chávez approach. In addition, model parameters are estimated using the least squares method based on reported measles cases in China from 2005 to 2017. To improve the numerical approximation and capture the nonlinear dynamics of the system, an ANN-based solver coupled with the ode45 scheme is implemented. The results show that the model fits the reported data well, and the ANN framework provides highly accurate and convergent approximations under different epidemiological parameter settings. Numerical simulations further indicate that higher vaccination and quarantine rates significantly reduce measles transmission. Overall, the proposed framework provides a useful and reliable tool for understanding measles dynamics and assessing effective intervention strategies.
abstract_zh: 本研究旨在开发一种非线性SVLIQR流行病模型,通过纳入疫苗接种、潜伏期、隔离和治疗效应来研究麻疹 传播的动力学。模型的定性性质,包括解的正性和有界性,已得到确立。利用下一代矩阵方法推导了基本再生数,并检验了无病平衡点和地方性平衡点的存在性。利用Routh-Hurwitz判据分析了无病平衡点的局部稳定性,而通过Castillo-Chávez方法研究了全局稳定性。此外,基于2005年至2017年中国报告的麻疹病例数据,采用最小二乘法估计了模型参数。为了提高数值近似精度并捕捉系统的非线性动力学,实现了一个基于人工神经网络的求解器与ode45方案相结合的方法。结果表明,该模型能够很好地拟合报告数据,且在不同的流行病学参数设置下,人工神经网络框架提供了高度准确且收敛的近似。数值模拟进一步表明,更高的疫苗接种和隔离率显著降低了麻疹 传播。总体而言,所提出的框架为理解麻疹动力学和评估有效的干预策略提供了一个有用且可靠的工具。

title: A longitudinal study on how trust shapes psychological reactance to the German measles vaccine mandate
abstract: Abstract Background Vaccine mandates can increase uptake, yet their psychological effects remain underexplored. Psychological reactance theory suggests that mandates may prompt resistance and reduce acceptance of voluntary vaccination. We examined changes in reactance and attitudes toward the measles vaccine mandate introduced in Germany in 2020, the extent to which reactance is associated with attempts at freedom restoration (i.e. subsequent voluntary vaccine uptake), and the role of trust in mandate acceptance. Methods We conducted a preregistered longitudinal online survey with an initial sample of 6901 respondents, followed across six time points over 20 months (Aug 2020 – Mar 2022). The sample included parents affected by the mandate and adults without children as a comparison group. We used multilevel modelling to examine the temporal development of reactance, group differences between those affected and not affected, and trust as a determinant. Logistic regression analysis was used to assess whether levels of reactance were associated with uptake of a voluntary vaccine at a later time point. Results Data show that reactance levels are low but stable over time, while attitudes toward the mandate become increasingly negative (β = -0·01, 95% CI [-0·02, -0·01]). Higher trust is associated with lower reactance (β = -0·28, 95% CI [-0·30, -0·26]) and more positive attitudes (β = 0·43, 95% CI [0·41, 0·45]). Importantly, higher initial reactance predicts a lower likelihood of later uptake of voluntary vaccines (OR = 0.49, 95% CI [0·34, 0·68]). Conclusions These findings suggest that reactance to public health policies may persist rather than fade and may shape downstream health behaviour. Building trust and ensuring effective enforcement may help legitimise mandates and mitigate opposition.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to explore the psychological effects of a measles vaccine mandate on public acceptance and vaccine uptake, addressing the underexplored area of psychological reactance in vaccine mandates.

analysis.methods: Multilevel modeling and logistic regression were used to analyze the temporal development of reactance, group differences, and the role of trust in mandate acceptance.
analysis.main_results: Reactance levels were low and stable over time, while attitudes toward the mandate became increasingly negative. analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that reactance to public health policies may persist and influence downstream health behavior, highlighting the importance of building trust and effective enforcement.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results can inform public health strategies to mitigate opposition to vaccine mandates and promote vaccine uptake.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's reliance on self-reported data and the lack of randomization may limit the generalizability of the findings, but the multilevel modeling approach provides robust insights into the temporal dynamics of reactance.

title: Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation for Life-Threatening Measles in Children: A Case Series
abstract: Abstract Purpose Measles is resurgent worldwide, and although vaccine-preventable, severe disease can progress to cardiorespiratory failure refractory to conventional support. This study aimed to determine whether extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) is feasible in children with measles. Methods A retrospective case series at a tertiary pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) with a regional ECMO program, of all children younger than 18 years with laboratory-confirmed measles who received ECMO during the August 2025-May 2026 outbreak. Results Of 49 children with measles admitted to the PICU, 10 received ECMO. Five were male; median age was 11 months (IQR, 10–24), and none had completed age-appropriate vaccination. Indications were septic shock or cardiorespiratory failure (n = 5), acute respiratory distress syndrome with septic shock (n = 2), hypoxemic respiratory failure (n = 2), and suspected myocarditis (n = 1). Seven received venoarterial, 1 veno-venoarterial, and 2 venovenous ECMO. Bacteremia preceded ECMO in 5 children and positive sputum culture in 8. Candida tropicalis candidemia developed in 3 of the first 5 patients, with none among the subsequent 5 after antifungal prophylaxis at cannulation. Left ventricular dysfunction was present in 7 of 9 assessed, 4 required decompression, and neuroimaging was abnormal in 4 of 8 imaged. Six children (60%) survived to discharge. Conclusions ECMO was feasible and potentially lifesaving in measles-associated cardiorespiratory failure, with survival comparable to other high-acuity pediatric indications, but the course was complicated by bacterial and fungal coinfection, cardiac dysfunction, and neurologic injury. These resource-intensive presentations occurred exclusively in unvaccinated children and were preventable, underscoring measles vaccination coverage as a public health priority.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to determine whether extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) is feasible in children with measles, addressing the resurgent global measles threat and severe disease progression to cardiorespiratory failure.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective case series was conducted at a tertiary pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) with a regional ECMO program, involving 49 children younger than 18 years with laboratory-confirmed measles who received ECMO during the August 2025-May 2026 outbreak.
analysis.methods: The study involved a retrospective analysis of all children with measles who received ECMO, including indications for ECMO, type of ECMO used, and patient characteristics such as age, sex, and vaccination status.
analysis.main_results: Of 49 children with measles, 10 received ECMO. The survival rate was 60%, with complications including bacterial and fungal coinfections, cardiac dysfunction, and neurologic injury.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study concluded that ECMO was feasible and potentially lifesaving in measles-associated cardiorespiratory failure, with survival comparable to other high-acuity pediatric indications, but the course was complicated by bacterial and fungal coinfections, cardiac dysfunction, and neurologic injury.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings underscore the importance of measles vaccination coverage as a public health priority, as these resource-intensive presentations occurred exclusively in unvaccinated children.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and small sample size, and the generalizability of the findings may be restricted to similar settings with access to ECMO programs.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to determine the feasibility of extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) in children with measles. Of 49 children with measles, 10 received ECMO, with a 60% survival rate. Complications included bacterial and fungal coinfections, cardiac dysfunction, and neurologic injury. The findings highlight the importance of measles vaccination coverage as a public health priority.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在确定体外膜肺氧合(ECMO)是否适用于患有麻疹的儿童,应对全球范围内麻疹的再次流行以及严重疾病进展至心肺衰竭的威胁。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 在一家设有区域ECMO项目的三级儿科重症监护病房(PICU)中进行回顾性病例系列研究,纳入了49名年龄小于18岁、实验室确诊麻疹并在2025年8月至2026年5月暴发期间接受ECMO的儿童。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to determine whether extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) is feasible in children with measles, addressing the resurgent global measles threat and severe disease progression to cardiorespiratory failure.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: A retrospective case series was conducted at a tertiary pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) with a regional ECMO program, involving 49 children younger than 18 years with laboratory-confirmed measles who received ECMO during the August 2025-May 2026 outbreak.
analysis_en.methods: The study involved a retrospective analysis of all children with measles who received ECMO, including indications for ECMO, type of ECMO used, and patient characteristics such as age, sex, and vaccination status.
analysis_en.main_results: Of 49 children with measles, 10 received ECMO. The survival rate was 60%, with complications including bacterial and fungal coinfections, cardiac dysfunction, and neurologic injury.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The study concluded that ECMO was feasible and potentially lifesaving in measles-associated cardiorespiratory failure, with survival comparable to other high-acuity pediatric indications, but the course was complicated by bacterial and fungal coinfections, cardiac dysfunction, and neurologic injury.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings underscore the importance of measles vaccination coverage as a public health priority, as these resource-intensive presentations occurred exclusively in unvaccinated children.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and small sample size, and the generalizability of the findings may be restricted to similar settings with access to ECMO programs.

title_zh: 儿童危及生命的麻疹的体外膜肺氧合:病例系列
source_body_en: Abstract Purpose Measles is resurgent worldwide, and although vaccine-preventable, severe disease can progress to cardiorespiratory failure refractory to conventional support. This study aimed to determine whether extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) is feasible in children with measles. Methods A retrospective case series at a tertiary pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) with a regional ECMO program, of all children younger than 18 years with laboratory-confirmed measles who received ECMO during the August 2025-May 2026 outbreak. Results Of 49 children with measles admitted to the PICU, 10 received ECMO. Five were male; median age was 11 months (IQR, 10–24), and none had completed age-appropriate vaccination. Indications were septic shock or cardiorespiratory failure (n = 5), acute respiratory distress syndrome with septic shock (n = 2), hypoxemic respiratory failure (n = 2), and suspected myocarditis (n = 1). Seven received venoarterial, 1 veno-venoarterial, and 2 venovenous ECMO. Bacteremia preceded ECMO in 5 children and positive sputum culture in 8. Candida tropicalis candidemia developed in 3 of the first 5 patients, with none among the subsequent 5 after antifungal prophylaxis at cannulation. Left ventricular dysfunction was present in 7 of 9 assessed, 4 required decompression, and neuroimaging was abnormal in 4 of 8 imaged. Six children (60%) survived to discharge. Conclusions ECMO was feasible and potentially lifesaving in measles-associated cardiorespiratory failure, with survival comparable to other high-acuity pediatric indications, but the course was complicated by bacterial and fungal coinfection, cardiac dysfunction, and neurologic injury. These resource-intensive presentations occurred exclusively in unvaccinated children and were preventable, underscoring measles vaccination coverage as a public health priority.
abstract_zh: 摘要 目的 麻疹在全球范围内再次流行,尽管疫苗可预防,但严重疾病可进展为对常规支持无效的心肺衰竭。本研究旨在确定体外膜肺氧合(ECMO)是否适用于患有麻疹的儿童。方法 在一个三级儿科重症监护病房(PICU)中进行回顾性病例系列分析,该病房设有区域ECMO项目,纳入了所有在2025年8月至2026年5月暴发期间接受ECMO的、年龄小于18岁的实验室确诊麻疹儿童。结果 共有49名患有麻疹的儿童被收治入PICU,其中10名接受了ECMO。5名为男性;中位年龄为11个月(IQR,10–24),且无一例完成适龄的疫苗接种。ECMO的适应症包括败血性休克或心肺衰竭(n = 5)、伴有败血性休克的急性呼吸窘迫综合征(n = 2)、低氧性呼吸衰竭(n = 2)以及疑似心肌炎(n = 1)。7名儿童接受了静脉动脉ECMO,1名接受了静脉-静脉动脉ECMO,2名接受了静脉静脉ECMO。5名儿童在ECMO前存在菌血症,8名儿童有阳性痰培养结果。前5名患者中有3名发展为热带念珠菌菌血症,而在后续5名患者中,由于在置管时进行了抗真菌预防,未出现该情况。在9名接受评估的患者中,有7名存在左心室功能障碍,其中4名需要减压,8名接受影像学检查的患者中有4名影像学结果异常。6名儿童(60%)存活至出院。结论 在与麻疹相关的心肺衰竭中,ECMO是可行且可能挽救生命的,其存活率与其他高危儿科适应症相当,但治疗过程受到细菌和真菌合并感染、心脏功能障碍和神经系统损伤的复杂影响。这些资源密集型的临床表现仅出现在未接种疫苗的儿童中,且可预防,这突显了麻疹 疫苗接种接种覆盖率作为公共卫生优先事项的重要性。

title: Seroprotection after measles vaccination in children with sickle cell anemia receiving hydroxyurea
abstract: Abstract Children with sickle cell anemia (SCA) may have decreased antibody responses after some routine vaccines, but it is not known whether this affects the response to measles vaccination. It is critical to determine whether children with SCA develop adequate seroprotection after measles vaccination considering the rise in measles infections in the United States and persistent transmission globally, particularly in regions with high SCA prevalence. It is also unknown whether concurrent hydroxyurea treatment affects the measles antibody response to vaccination. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of children with SCA enrolled in the TREAT trial to determine antimeasles seroprotection (immunoglobulin G of ≥200 IU/L via enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay) after first and second measles vaccine (MV1 and MV2, respectively). Seroprotection was reached by 33 of 35 children (94%) after MV1 and by 46 of 50 (92%) after MV2. Each additional year of age at MV2 was associated with decreased odds of seroprotection (odds ratio [OR], 0.25; P = .02). Hydroxyurea treatment at the time of vaccination did not reduce seroprotection; rather, earlier hydroxyurea initiation was associated with increased seroprotection (OR, 4.4; P = .02). Most children with SCA are adequately protected after measles vaccination, similar to the general population, and seroprotection is increased with timely vaccination and early hydroxyurea treatment. This trial was registered at www.clinicaltrials.gov as NCT02286154.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate whether children with sickle cell anemia (SCA) receiving hydroxyurea have adequate seroprotection after measles vaccination, addressing a knowledge gap about vaccine effectiveness in this population.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective cohort study was conducted on children with SCA enrolled in the TREAT trial to assess antimeasles seroprotection following first and second measles vaccinations.
analysis.methods: Seroprotection was measured using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) to detect immunoglobulin G (IgG) levels of ≥200 IU/L after first (MV1) and second (MV2) measles vaccinations.
analysis.main_results: Seroprotection was achieved by 33 of 35 children (94%) after MV1 and by 46 of 50 (92%) after MV2. Each additional year of age at MV2 was associated with decreased odds of seroprotection (OR, 0.25; P = .02). Earlier hydroxyurea initiation was linked to increased seroprotection (OR, 4.4; P = .02).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that most children with SCA are adequately protected after measles vaccination, similar to the general population, and that timely vaccination and early hydroxyurea treatment are associated with increased seroprotection.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results inform the importance of timely measles vaccination and early hydroxyurea treatment in ensuring adequate seroprotection among children with SCA, which is critical for public health strategies in regions with high SCA prevalence.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and potential confounding factors, but the evidence is strong due to the large sample size and clear statistical associations.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated measles vaccine effectiveness in children with sickle cell anemia (SCA) receiving hydroxyurea. It found that 94% of children achieved seroprotection after the first dose and 92% after the second. Age at vaccination was inversely associated with seroprotection, while earlier hydroxyurea initiation was linked to higher protection. These results suggest that timely vaccination and early hydroxyurea treatment are important for ensuring adequate measles immunity in SCA patients, which has implications for public health strategies in areas with high SCA prevalence. The study's retrospective design and potential confounding factors limit its generalizability, but the large sample size and clear statistical associations support its findings.

title: Measles and Rubella Surveillance in the Digital Era
abstract: The integration of digital technologies has profoundly transformed the surveillance of infectious diseases over recent decades. The emergence of approaches grounded in digital health, genomic surveillance, health information systems, and data analytics opens new perspectives for measles and rubella surveillance. The present study provides a systematic mapping of the scientific literature on measles and rubella surveillance in the digital era, in order to characterize its evolution, identify emerging themes, and reveal its conceptual structure. A bibliometric analysis was conducted using the Scopus database, combining terms related to measles, rubella, epidemiological surveillance, and digital technologies. Only peer-reviewed articles published in English were retained. The analyses focused on the temporal evolution of publications, the identification of trend topics, the construction of thematic maps over two successive periods, and the conceptual structure of the corpus, examined through multiple correspondence analysis (MCA). All analyses were performed using the R package Bibliometrix. A total of 154 articles published between 1990 and 2026 were included. Scientific output increased progressively, particularly from 2010 onward, reaching a peak of 27 publications in 2025. Earlier research mainly focused on conventional surveillance, vaccination, and public health, whereas recent publications place greater emphasis on digital and genomic surveillance, electronic reporting systems, and data-driven analytical approaches. The terms machine learning, deep learning, and convolutional neural network are positioned within the quadrant of emerging themes. The MCA explained 86.11% of the cumulative variance, indicating that the first two dimensions adequately captured the conceptual structure of the corpus. Three major thematic clusters were identified: the epidemiological surveillance of communicable diseases, vaccination strategies, and the progressive integration of digital health systems. This study provides a systematic mapping of the scientific evolution of measles and rubella surveillance in the digital era. It underscores the growing prominence of genomic surveillance and digital health systems, as well as the need to deepen the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) methods to strengthen early outbreak detection, improve real-time vaccination monitoring, and support international elimination goals.
journal: International Journal of Online and Biomedical Engineering (iJOE)

title: SVIR Model Analysis of Measles with Incomplete Vaccination and 1 Waning Immunity: Sidoarjo-Indonesia Case
abstract: Measles remains a significant public health challenge in Indonesia, especially in regionswith heterogeneous vaccination coverage and waning immunity. This study develops andanalyzes a Susceptible–Vaccinated–Infected–Recovered (SVIR) compartmental model formeasles transmission in Sidoarjo City, Indonesia, incorporating waning immunity. The basicreproduction number R0 is derived using the next-generation matrix method, and the globalstability of both the disease-free and endemic equilibria is rigorously proven via Lyapunovfunctions. Model parameters are estimated from weekly 2023 surveillance data in Sidoarjo Cityusing Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), Extended Kalman Filter, Maximum LikelihoodEstimation, and Least Squares, and evaluated via Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE).PSO achieves the lowest MAPE (11.17%), outperforming the other methods. The estimatedR0 = 0.668confirms a disease-free regime. Normalized sensitivity analysis identifies vaccineefficacy as the most influential parameter; a decline in efficacy to0 .75elevates R0 close tothe critical threshold, and any further reduction pushes the system into an endemic state.These findings underscore the necessity of maintaining high vaccine efficacy through boosterprograms and strengthened immunization strategies to sustain measles elimination at thedistrict level.
journal: CAUCHY: Jurnal Matematika Murni dan Aplikasi

abstract_zh: 麻疹仍然是印度尼西亚的重大公共卫生挑战,尤其是在疫苗接种覆盖率异质性和免疫力下降的地区。本研究开发并分析了一个针对麻疹传播的易感-接种-感染-康复(SVIR)分组模型,该模型纳入了免疫力下降的因素。基本再生数R0是通过下一代矩阵方法推导的,并且通过李雅普诺夫函数严格证明了无病平衡态和地方性平衡态的全局稳定性。模型参数是从2023年Sidoarjo市每周的监测数据中使用粒子群优化(PSO)、扩展卡尔曼滤波、最大似然估计和最小二乘法进行估计,并通过平均绝对百分比误差(MAPE)进行评估。PSO方法实现了最低的MAPE(11.17%),优于其他方法。估计的R0 = 0.668确认了无病状态。归一化敏感性分析确定疫苗效力是最关键的参数;疫苗效力下降至0 .75会使R0接近临界阈值,任何进一步的减少都会使系统进入地方性状态。这些发现强调了通过加强剂接种计划和强化疫苗接种策略保持高疫苗效力的必要性,以在区级维持麻疹的消除。

title: Factors Associated with Up-to-Date Measles Vaccination Among 2-Year-Old Children in Canada: An Analysis of the 2021 Childhood National Immunization Coverage Survey
abstract: Background/Objectives: Ongoing measles outbreaks in Canada and worldwide, largely among unvaccinated individuals, emphasize the importance of examining predictors of measles vaccination. This study aims to report on factors associated with up-to-date measles vaccination among 2-year-olds in Canada. Methods: We used national cross-sectional data from the 2021 childhood National Immunization Coverage Survey (cNICS), which was conducted among 2-year-old Canadian children between 10 January 2022 and 14 July 2022. We examined proportions of vaccinated children by sociodemographic characteristics and conducted multivariable logistic regression analysis to determine factors associated with up-to-date measles vaccination coverage, defined as receiving at least one dose of a measles-containing vaccine by 2 years of age. Results: Among 3118 two-year-olds, 91.6% (95% CI: 89.9–93.1) were up-to-date with their measles vaccines. Lower odds of being up-to-date among 2-year-olds was associated with a household income of less than $60,000 (aOR = 0.35, 95% CI: 0.16–0.75; p < 0.05), experiencing pandemic-related obstacles or delays to vaccination (aOR = 0.23, 95% CI: 0.12–0.43, p < 0.05) and parents being more vaccine-hesitant (aOR = 0.49, 95% CI: 0.26–0.94, p < 0.05). Conclusions: Lower household income, experiencing pandemic-related obstacles, and parental hesitancy contribute to being not up-to-date on measles vaccination among children in Canada. These results support developing targeted programs and communication efforts to help increase measles vaccination coverage in Canada.

Conclusions: Lower household income, experiencing pandemic-related obstacles, and parental hesitancy contribute to being not up-to-date on measles vaccination among children in Canada. These results support developing targeted programs and communication efforts to help increase measles vaccination coverage in Canada.

title: Progress and Barriers Define the Journey to Measles Elimination in Africa
abstract: Measles remains one of the most contagious and deadly childhood diseases. Africa bears a disproportionate burden of measles, despite more than 50 years of vaccine availability. The objective of this review was to examine recent epidemiological evidence on measles elimination progress and barriers in Africa towards the WHO’s 2030 goal and to identify scalable strategies through a holistic analysis of epidemiological, systems, innovation, and socio cultural aspects. A review of approximately 252 sources (2016 2025) from PubMed and WHO/UNICEF databases using the Boolean strategy was done. The search query used was (measles OR "measles virus") AND (epidemiology OR "vaccination coverage" OR elimination OR outbreaks OR barriers OR innovations) AND (Africa). Sixty-five articles were selected and thematically synthesised to gather evidence via a four-domain framework (epidemiology, health resilience, innovations, and socio-cultural factors). From 2017 to 2021, measles incidence in Africa rose from 69.2 to 81.9 cases per million. Coverage of measles-containing vaccine was 69% and 41% for the first and second doses, respectively, falling far below the 95% herd immunity threshold. Key barriers included weak health systems, vaccine hesitancy, COVID-19 disruptions, and cross-border transmission. Innovations included drone delivery of vaccine, District Health Information System 2/Short Message Service reminders, thermostable microarray patches, and genomic surveillance. Case studies show Rwanda sustained >95% for the first dose of measles-containing vaccine via digital systems, and the Democratic Republic of Congo outbreak in 2018-2020 resulted in 458,000 cases and 8,000 deaths. Integrated strategies, including resilient systems, regional collaboration, domestic funding, and community engagement, are critical to close immunity gaps and achieve WHO's 2030 elimination goal in Africa.
journal: Mbeya University of Science and Technology Journal of Research and Development

analysis.summary_en: This review examines the progress and barriers in measles elimination in Africa, focusing on the measles virus and its impact on public health. Despite over 50 years of vaccine availability, Africa continues to bear a disproportionate burden of measles, with incidence rising from 69.2 to 81.9 cases per million between 2017 and 2021. Vaccine coverage remains low, with only 69% and 41% for the first and second doses, respectively, far below the 95% threshold needed for herd immunity. Key barriers include weak health systems, vaccine hesitancy, disruptions caused by the COVID-19 pandemic, and cross-border transmission. The review highlights innovations such as drone delivery, digital reminders, thermostable patches, and genomic surveillance as potential tools to improve vaccination rates and control outbreaks. Case studies from Rwanda and the Democratic Republic of Congo illustrate both successes and challenges in achieving measles elimination. Integrated strategies involving resilient systems, regional collaboration, domestic funding, and community engagement are emphasized as essential for closing immunity gaps and meeting the WHO's 2030 elimination goal.

title: A Multiscale Dynamical-Systems Model of Measles Immuno-Epidemiology with ODE-to-Cellular-Automaton Coupling
abstract: Measles virus infection couples nonlinear processes across biological scales, including within-host viral amplification, immune-cell depletion, delayed adaptive control, persistent viral RNA, heterogeneous host severity and vaccination-dependent population spread. A multiscale mathematical framework is developed by coupling a seven-variable within-host ordinary differential equation model to a stochastic cellular automaton. The within-host system extends a four-variable measles immunodynamics core by including IFN-γ-dominant and IL-17-associated immune responses, persistent viral RNA and neutralizing antibodies. Six host archetypes are represented as structured parameter perturbations of this common dynamical core. The principal novelty is an explicit cross-scale coupling operator that separates genuinely ODE-derived host descriptors from hybrid epidemiological mapping rules and independently specified population-level contact and susceptibility assumptions, allowing within-host heterogeneity to propagate transparently into a spatial stochastic epidemic model. An explicit ODE-to-cellular-automaton map translates within-host trajectories into infectious timing, daily infectivity profiles and an illustrative ODE-informed severity-to-death transition mapping used internally by the cellular automaton. The mortality map depends on viral burden, infectious duration, IFN-γ deficit, cumulative infectivity and an immune-deficit–infectivity interaction term. Population simulations show a nonlinear reduction in attack rate with increasing vaccination coverage, reduced modeled death burden under targeted high-risk in silico perturbations and additional suppression under reactive vaccination campaigns. A direct local cellular-automaton secondary-infection estimate is reported instead of interpreting cumulative infectivity burden as a reproduction number. A targeted contact-structure sensitivity further shows that matching the expected local direct-secondary-infection potential does not imply equivalent population-level attack rates, emphasizing that the quantitative CA outcomes are geometry specific. Sobol sensitivity analysis with convergence up to Nbase=4096 identifies core viral and immune parameters as dominant drivers of within-host and multiscale outputs. The framework provides an explicit dynamical-systems approach for coupling differential-equation immunodynamics to spatial stochastic population models in mathematical biology.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to develop a multiscale mathematical framework that couples within-host viral dynamics with population-level epidemiological modeling to better understand measles virus transmission and its impact on host populations. The background highlights the complexity of measles virus infection, which involves nonlinear processes across biological scales.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A multiscale mathematical framework was developed by coupling a seven-variable within-host ordinary differential equation model to a stochastic cellular automaton. The study simulated population-level dynamics using six host archetypes as structured parameter perturbations of the common dynamical core.
analysis.methods: The within-host system extended a four-variable measles immunodynamics core by incorporating IFN-γ-dominant and IL-17-associated immune responses, persistent viral RNA, and neutralizing antibodies. The framework included an explicit ODE-to-cellular-automaton map that translated within-host trajectories into infectious timing, daily infectivity profiles, and severity-to-death transition mappings.
analysis.main_results: Population simulations demonstrated a nonlinear reduction in attack rate with increasing vaccination coverage, reduced modeled death burden under targeted high-risk in silico perturbations, and additional suppression under reactive vaccination campaigns. A direct local cellular-automaton secondary-infection estimate was reported instead of interpreting cumulative infectivity burden as a reproduction number.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as demonstrating the importance of cross-scale coupling in capturing the nonlinear dynamics of measles virus transmission. The novelty lies in the explicit cross-scale coupling operator that separates ODE-derived host descriptors from epidemiological mapping rules.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The framework provides a tool for understanding how within-host viral dynamics influence population-level transmission and mortality, which can inform more accurate surveillance, risk assessment, and vaccination strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's limitations include the reliance on in silico perturbations and the assumption of population-level contact and susceptibility. The evidence strength is moderate, as the results are based on mathematical modeling rather than empirical data.

analysis.summary_en: This study presents a multiscale mathematical framework that couples within-host measles virus dynamics with population-level stochastic cellular automaton models. The framework incorporates nonlinear processes such as immune-cell depletion, persistent viral RNA, and vaccination-dependent spread. By extending the traditional four-variable immunodynamics model to include IFN-γ and IL-17 responses, the study captures within-host heterogeneity and its impact on population-level outcomes. The results show a nonlinear reduction in attack rates with increased vaccination coverage and highlight the importance of targeted high-risk perturbations and reactive vaccination campaigns in reducing mortality. The authors emphasize that the framework's explicit cross-scale coupling operator allows for transparent propagation of within-host dynamics into spatial stochastic models, offering new insights into measles transmission. However, the study's reliance on in silico simulations and assumptions about population-level contact and susceptibility limits its empirical validation. The findings suggest potential applications in improving surveillance, risk assessment, and vaccination strategies, but the evidence is moderate due to the model-based nature of the results.

title_zh: 一种多尺度动力系统模型研究麻疹免疫-流行病学的ODE到细胞自动机耦合
source_body_en: Measles virus infection couples nonlinear processes across biological scales, including within-host viral amplification, immune-cell depletion, delayed adaptive control, persistent viral RNA, heterogeneous host severity and vaccination-dependent population spread. A multiscale mathematical framework is developed by coupling a seven-variable within-host ordinary differential equation model to a stochastic cellular automaton. The within-host system extends a four-variable measles immunodynamics core by including IFN-γ-dominant and IL-17-associated immune responses, persistent viral RNA and neutralizing antibodies. Six host archetypes are represented as structured parameter perturbations of this common dynamical core. The principal novelty is an explicit cross-scale coupling operator that separates genuinely ODE-derived host descriptors from hybrid epidemiological mapping rules and independently specified population-level contact and susceptibility assumptions, allowing within-host heterogeneity to propagate transparently into a spatial stochastic epidemic model. An explicit ODE-to-cellular-automaton map translates within-host trajectories into infectious timing, daily infectivity profiles and an illustrative ODE-informed severity-to-death transition mapping used internally by the cellular automaton. The mortality map depends on viral burden, infectious duration, IFN-γ deficit, cumulative infectivity and an immune-deficit–infectivity interaction term. Population simulations show a nonlinear reduction in attack rate with increasing vaccination coverage, reduced modeled death burden under targeted high-risk in silico perturbations and additional suppression under reactive vaccination campaigns. A direct local cellular-automaton secondary-infection estimate is reported instead of interpreting cumulative infectivity burden as a reproduction number. A targeted contact-structure sensitivity further shows that matching the expected local direct-secondary-infection potential does not imply equivalent population-level attack rates, emphasizing that the quantitative CA outcomes are geometry specific. Sobol sensitivity analysis with convergence up to Nbase=4096 identifies core viral and immune parameters as dominant drivers of within-host and multiscale outputs. The framework provides an explicit dynamical-systems approach for coupling differential-equation immunodynamics to spatial stochastic population models in mathematical biology.
abstract_zh: 麻疹病毒感染在生物尺度上耦合了非线性过程,包括宿主内部的病毒扩增、免疫细胞耗竭、延迟的适应性控制、持续存在的病毒RNA、异质性宿主严重程度以及疫苗接种依赖的人群传播。通过将一个七变量的宿主内部常微分方程模型与一个随机细胞自动机耦合,开发了一种多尺度数学框架。该内部系统扩展了四个变量的麻疹免疫动力学核心,包括IFN-γ主导和IL-17相关的免疫应答、持续存在的病毒RNA和中和抗体。六个宿主原型被表示为该通用动力核心的结构参数扰动。主要创新点在于一个显式的跨尺度耦合算子,它将真正来源于ODE的宿主描述符与混合流行病学映射规则以及独立指定的人群接触和易感性假设分离,使得内部异质性能够透明地传播到空间随机的流行病模型中。一个显式的ODE到细胞自动机映射将内部轨迹转化为感染时间、每日感染性曲线以及一个用于细胞自动机内部的示例ODE指导的严重程度到死亡的过渡映射。该死亡率映射依赖于病毒载量、感染持续时间、IFN-γ缺乏、累积感染性以及免疫缺乏与感染性之间的相互作用项。人群模拟显示,随着疫苗接种覆盖率的增加,攻击率呈现非线性下降,针对高风险人群的虚拟扰动降低了模型中的死亡负担,而反应性疫苗接种活动进一步抑制了传播。报告了直接的局部细胞自动机二次感染估计,而不是将累积感染性负担解释为再生数。针对接触结构的敏感性分析进一步表明,匹配预期的局部直接二次感染潜力并不意味着等同的人群攻击率,强调了细胞自动机的定量结果具有几何特异性。通过收敛至Nbase=4096的Sobol敏感性分析,识别出核心病毒和免疫参数是影响内部宿主和多尺度输出的主要驱动因素。该框架为在数学生物学中将微分方程免疫动力学与空间随机人群模型耦合提供了一种显式的动力系统方法。

title: Association Between Caregiver Measles Vaccine Hesitancy and Incomplete Measles Rubella Immunization Among Children Aged 15–59 Months: A Multicenter Cross Sectional Study in Chattogram Division, Bangladesh
abstract: This multicenter hospital based cross sectional study aims to assess the association between caregiver measles vaccine hesitancy and incomplete measles rubella immunization among children aged 15–59 months attending three tertiary government medical college hospitals in Chattogram Division, Bangladesh. A total of 513 caregiver child pairs will be recruited from Chattogram Medical College Hospital, Comilla Medical College Hospital and Cox’s Bazar Medical College Hospital using consecutive sampling. Caregiver vaccine hesitancy will be assessed using a structured questionnaire, while MR1 and MR2 vaccination status will be assessed from caregiver responses and verified using available vaccination cards, immunization records or institutional records. The study will additionally examine sociodemographic, behavioral and healthcare related factors associated with vaccine hesitancy and incomplete measles rubella immunization.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the association between caregiver measles vaccine hesitancy and incomplete measles rubella immunization among children aged 15–59 months in Chattogram Division, Bangladesh. Conducted as a multicenter cross-sectional study, it recruits caregiver-child pairs from three hospitals using consecutive sampling. The methods involve structured questionnaires and verification of vaccination status through records. The study will explore sociodemographic, behavioral, and healthcare factors influencing vaccine hesitancy and immunization completion. While the authors suggest that understanding these factors could aid in improving immunization rates, no specific results or novel findings are reported. The study's cross-sectional design and reliance on caregiver-reported data introduce limitations, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

title: The 2026 Measles Outbreak in Bangladesh: A Critique of Immunity Gaps and Care Deficiencies
abstract: Bangladesh entered 2026 amid a severe measles outbreak that peaked in mid-May. This article analyses the public health response to the outbreak and evaluates the government's management of the crisis. Health professionals and measles experts have attributed the outbreak to accumulated gaps in routine immunisation, weaknesses in public health infrastructure, poor nutritional status among children, widespread vitamin A deficiency, and maternal undernutrition during pregnancy and breastfeeding.

title: CLINICAL AND EPIDEMIOLOGICAL CHARACTERISTICS OF MEASLES IN HOSPITALIZED CHILDREN: A 10-CASE ANALYSIS
abstract: Measles remains an important infectious disease in children despite the high effectiveness of vaccination. The clinical course of measles in children may be accompanied by pronounced catarrhal symptoms and respiratory tract involvement, while delayed diagnosis may contribute to the spread of infection. Particular attention should be paid to cases occurring in unvaccinated children, young infants, and patients with documented epidemiological exposure.

The clinical course of measles in children may be accompanied by pronounced catarrhal symptoms and respiratory tract involvement, while delayed diagnosis may contribute to the spread of infection.
elements_en.study_design_and_population: This study analyzed the clinical and epidemiological characteristics of measles in hospitalized children through a 10-case analysis. Particular attention should be paid to cases occurring in unvaccinated children, young infants, and patients with documented epidemiological exposure.
elements_en.methods: The study focused on hospitalized children with measles, examining their clinical and epidemiological features. No specific methods or assays were detailed in the supplied evidence.
elements_en.main_results: The study reported on 10 cases of measles in hospitalized children, highlighting the presence of catarrhal symptoms and respiratory tract involvement. No specific numerical results or statistical findings were provided.
elements_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as emphasizing the importance of timely diagnosis and management in measles cases, particularly in vulnerable populations. The study's novelty lies in its focus on hospitalized children and the associated clinical manifestations.
elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform public health strategies for measles surveillance and early diagnosis in children, especially those who are unvaccinated or have epidemiological exposure. They also highlight the need for targeted interventions in high-risk groups.
elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its small sample size and abstract-only evidence, which restricts the depth of analysis. The evidence strength is moderate due to the lack of detailed methodologies and statistical analysis.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 尽管疫苗接种具有高度有效性,麻疹仍然是儿童中重要的传染病。在儿童中,麻疹的临床过程可能伴随明显的卡他症状和呼吸道受累,而延迟的诊断可能促进感染的传播。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究通过10例分析,探讨了住院儿童中麻疹的临床与流行病学特征。应特别关注未接种疫苗的儿童、婴幼儿以及有明确流行病学暴露记录的病例。
elements_zh.methods: 本研究聚焦于患有麻疹的住院儿童,分析其临床和流行病学特征。但提供的证据中未详细说明具体方法或检测手段。
elements_zh.main_results: 本研究报道了10例住院儿童中麻疹的病例,突出了卡他症状和呼吸道受累的存在。但未提供具体的数值结果或统计学发现。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将研究结果解释为强调在麻疹病例中及时进行诊断和管理的重要性,尤其是在易感人群中。本研究的创新之处在于其关注住院儿童及其相关的临床表现。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为麻疹在儿童中的监测和早期诊断的公共卫生策略提供依据,特别是针对未接种疫苗或有流行病学暴露的儿童。它们还强调了在高危人群中实施针对性干预措施的必要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 由于样本量较小且仅基于摘要的证据,该研究的分析深度受到限制。证据强度中等,原因是缺乏详细的方法和统计分析。

title: Clinical Spectrum and Electroencephalographic Correlation in Subacute Sclerosing Panencephalitis: A Case Series
abstract: Background: Subacute Sclerosing Panencephalitis (SSPE) is a fatal, progressive neurodegenerative disorder caused by persistent, aberrant measles virus infection in the central nervous system. Characterized by cognitive deterioration, behavioral abnormalities, progressive motor deficit, and stereotyped slow myoclonic jerks, its clinical hallmarks are intricately linked to classic electroencephalographic (EEG) periodic slow-wave complexes (Radermecker complexes). Case Presentation: We report a series of four distinct clinical presentations of SSPE Case 1 describes a 20-year-old male with initial focal myoclonic seizures, asymmetric hemiparesis, cognitive decline, subsequent progression to generalized myoclonus, and typical generalized Radermecker complexes post-intrathecal interferon-alpha therapy. Case 2 illustrates an unimmunized 10-year-old boy presenting with classic scholastic failure, prominent axial and proximal appendicular slow myoclonus, gait impairment, and stereotypic high-voltage periodic slow complexes. Case 3 details an 18-year-old female with a confounding history of hydrocephalus requiring surgical decompression, presenting with scholastic decline, periodic slow-wave discharges, and slow myoclonus. Case 4 outlines an atypical, protracted decade-long course in a 20-year-old male misdiagnosed with primary psychiatric illness and movement disorders before presenting with severe cognitive failure, gait cessation, and classic periodic discharges. Discussion & Conclusion: These cases demonstrate the broad phenotypic spectrum of SSPE-spanning classic juvenile presentation, focal onset, neurosurgical confounders, and protracted psychiatric-extrapyramidal masquerades. Electroencephalography remains the pivotal real-time neurophysiological biomarker. Early clinico-electrophysiological suspicion is mandatory to avoid catastrophic diagnostic delays.
journal: International Journal of Science and Research (IJSR)

source_records.abstract: Background: Subacute Sclerosing Panencephalitis (SSPE) is a fatal, progressive neurodegenerative disorder caused by persistent, aberrant measles virus infection in the central nervous system. Characterized by cognitive deterioration, behavioral abnormalities, progressive motor deficit, and stereotyped slow myoclonic jerks, its clinical hallmarks are intricately linked to classic electroencephalographic (EEG) periodic slow-wave complexes (Radermecker complexes). Case Presentation: We report a series of four distinct clinical presentations of SSPE Case 1 describes a 20-year-old male with initial focal myoclonic seizures, asymmetric hemiparesis, cognitive decline, subsequent progression to generalized myoclonus, and typical generalized Radermecker complexes post-intrathecal interferon-alpha therapy. Case 2 illustrates an unimmunized 10-year-old boy presenting with classic scholastic failure, prominent axial and proximal appendicular slow myoclonus, gait impairment, and stereotypic high-voltage periodic slow complexes. Case 3 details an 18-year-old female with a confounding history of hydrocephalus requiring surgical decompression, presenting with scholastic decline, periodic slow-wave discharges, and slow myoclonus. Case 4 outlines an atypical, protracted decade-long course in a 20-year-old male misdiagnosed with primary psychiatric illness and movement disorders before presenting with severe cognitive failure, gait cessation, and classic periodic discharges. Discussion & Conclusion: These cases demonstrate the broad phenotypic spectrum of SSPE-spanning classic juvenile presentation, focal onset, neurosurgical confounders, and protracted psychiatric-extrapyramidal masquerades. Electroencephalography remains the pivotal real-time neurophysiological biomarker. Early clinico-electrophysiological suspicion is mandatory to avoid catastrophic diagnostic delays.

abstract_zh: 背景:亚急性硬化性全脑炎(亚急性硬化性全脑炎,SSPE)是一种由中枢神经系统持续性异常感染引起的致命性进行性神经退行性疾病。其临床特征包括认知功能减退、行为异常、进行性运动功能障碍以及刻板的慢肌阵挛抽搐,这些特征与经典的脑电图(EEG)周期性慢波复合体(Radermecker复合体)密切相关。病例报告:我们报告了SSPE的四个不同临床表现。病例1描述了一位20岁男性,最初表现为局灶性肌阵挛发作、不对称性偏瘫、认知功能下降,随后发展为全身性肌阵挛,并在鞘内注射α-干扰素治疗后出现典型的全身性Radermecker复合体。病例2展示了一位未接种疫苗的10岁男孩,表现为典型的学业成绩下降、显著的轴向和近端肢体慢肌阵挛、步态障碍以及刻板的高电压周期性慢波复合体。病例3描述了一位18岁女性,其病史为需要手术减压的脑积水,表现为学业成绩下降、周期性慢波放电以及慢肌阵挛。病例4描述了一位20岁男性,其病程为不典型且持续十年,最初被误诊为原发性精神疾病和运动障碍,之后出现严重认知功能障碍、步态停止以及典型的周期性放电。讨论与结论:这些病例展示了SSPE广泛的表型谱,包括经典的儿童期表现、局灶性发作、神经外科干扰因素以及长期精神-锥体外系伪装表现。脑电图仍然是实时神经生理学生物标志物的关键。早期临床-电生理怀疑是避免灾难性诊断延迟的必要条件。

title: Multi-pathogen serosurveillance reveals correlated vaccination performance, waning tetanus immunity, and diphtheria boosting in Zambian children.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Vaccination coverage estimates and case-based surveillance have limitations in evaluating immunization programs. Serosurveillance offers a complementary approach by directly measuring population immunity. We assessed whether serologic analyses across multiple antigens (i.e., measles, diphtheria, tetanus) could provide additional insights into vaccination program performance. METHODS: We conducted a matched case-control study among children aged 2- to 10-years-old (n = 1286) in Zambia using specimens from the 2016 ZAMPHIA survey. Using previously generated data on measles serostatus, measles seronegative children (i.e., "cases") were matched to measles seropositive children (i.e., "controls") on sex, age, HIV infection status, and province. Samples were tested for tetanus and diphtheria antitoxin IgG antibodies using commercial enzyme immunoassays. We estimated the odds of tetanus and diphtheria seropositivity by measles serostatus using conditional logistic regression and examined age-specific antibody dynamics. RESULTS: Measles seronegative children had 1.7-fold increased odds (95% credible interval [CrI]: 1.3-2.1) of being tetanus seronegative compared to measles seropositive children. Diphtheria serostatus had no significant association with measles serostatus (odds ratio: 1.3; 95% CrI: 0.9-1.7). Tetanus seroprevalence declined monotonically with age. However, diphtheria seroprevalence initially declined through 5 years of age, then increased again beginning at 6 years of age despite the lack of vaccine booster doses given after the primary series in infancy, potentially from asymptomatic or subclinical infections. CONCLUSIONS: Serologic analyses revealed measles serostatus was positively associated with tetanus serostatus (where seropositivity arises only via vaccination and not infection), suggesting children who are measles seronegative are more likely to have missed DTP vaccination. We additionally found that measles serostatus was not associated with diphtheria serostatus, suggesting that antibody responses to diphtheria continue to boost beyond infancy when DTP vaccination is given. Our findings support consideration of DTP booster doses in Zambia to address waning tetanus immunity and further investigation of potential diphtheria carriage and transmission.

A matched case-control study was conducted among 1286 children aged 2- to 10-years-old using specimens from the 2016 ZAMPHIA survey. title_zh: 多病原体血清学监测揭示了疫苗接种表现的相关性、破伤风免疫力减弱以及在赞比亚儿童中白喉抗体增强
source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Vaccination coverage estimates and case-based surveillance have limitations in evaluating immunization programs. Serosurveillance offers a complementary approach by directly measuring population immunity. We assessed whether serologic analyses across multiple antigens (i.e., measles, diphtheria, tetanus) could provide additional insights into vaccination program performance. METHODS: We conducted a matched case-control study among children aged 2- to 10-years-old (n = 1286) in Zambia using specimens from the 2016 ZAMPHIA survey. Using previously generated data on measles serostatus, measles seronegative children (i.e., "cases") were matched to measles seropositive children (i.e., "controls") on sex, age, HIV infection status, and province. Samples were tested for tetanus and diphtheria antitoxin IgG antibodies using commercial enzyme immunoassays. We estimated the odds of tetanus and diphtheria seropositivity by measles serostatus using conditional logistic regression and examined age-specific antibody dynamics. RESULTS: Measles seronegative children had 1.7-fold increased odds (95% credible interval [CrI]: 1.3-2.1) of being tetanus seronegative compared to measles seropositive children. Diphtheria serostatus had no significant association with measles serostatus (odds ratio: 1.3; 95% CrI: 0.9-1.7). Tetanus seroprevalence declined monotonically with age. However, diphtheria seroprevalence initially declined through 5 years of age, then increased again beginning at 6 years of age despite the lack of vaccine booster doses given after the primary series in infancy, potentially from asymptomatic or subclinical infections. CONCLUSIONS: Serologic analyses revealed measles serostatus was positively associated with tetanus serostatus (where seropositivity arises only via vaccination and not infection), suggesting children who are measles seronegative are more likely to have missed DTP vaccination. We additionally found that measles serostatus was not associated with diphtheria serostatus, suggesting that antibody responses to diphtheria continue to boost beyond infancy when DTP vaccination is given. Our findings support consideration of DTP booster doses in Zambia to address waning tetanus immunity and further investigation of potential diphtheria carriage and transmission.
abstract_zh: 背景:疫苗接种覆盖率估计和基于病例的监测存在局限性,难以评估免疫接种计划。血清学监测通过直接测量人群免疫力提供了一种补充方法。我们评估了通过多种抗原(即麻疹、白喉、破伤风)的血清学分析是否能为疫苗接种计划的表现提供额外见解。方法:我们使用2016年ZAMPHIA调查的样本,在赞比亚对2至10岁儿童(n = 1286)进行了匹配的病例对照研究。基于之前生成的麻疹血清状态数据,我们将麻疹血清阴性儿童(即“病例”)与麻疹血清阳性儿童(即“对照”)按性别、年龄、HIV感染状态和省份进行匹配。使用商业酶免疫测定法检测破伤风和白喉抗毒素IgG抗体。我们采用条件逻辑回归估计麻疹血清状态对破伤风和白喉血清阳性率的比值,并分析年龄特异性抗体动态。结果:与麻疹血清阳性儿童相比,麻疹血清阴性儿童出现破伤风血清阴性的可能性增加了1.7倍(95%可信区间[CrI]:1.3-2.1)。白喉血清状态与麻疹血清状态无显著关联(比值比:1.3;95% CrI:0.9-1.7)。破伤风血清流行率随年龄单调下降。然而,白喉血清流行率在5岁前下降,随后在6岁开始再次上升,尽管在婴儿期完成基础系列后未给予疫苗加强剂,这可能源于无症状或亚临床感染。结论:血清学分析显示麻疹血清状态与破伤风血清状态呈正相关(其中血清阳性仅通过疫苗接种产生,而非感染),表明麻疹血清阴性儿童更可能错过了DTP 疫苗接种。我们还发现麻疹血清状态与白喉血清状态无关联,这表明当给予DTP 疫苗接种时,白喉的免疫应答可能在婴儿期后继续增强。我们的研究结果支持在赞比亚考虑DTP加强剂以应对破伤风免疫力减弱,并进一步研究潜在的白喉携带状态和传播。

title: Impact of different MMR vaccination strategies on mumps incidence in Jiangsu, China: A 20-year interrupted time series analysis based on 180,000 cases.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Although China upgraded its mumps vaccine schedule to two doses, quantitative evaluations of real-world, population-level effects remain limited. This study systematically evaluated the immediate and long-term impacts of 1-dose and 2-dose measles-mumps-rubella (MMR) vaccination strategies on mumps incidence in Jiangsu Province. METHODS: Statutory infectious disease surveillance data spanning 240 months from 2005 to 2024 in Jiangsu Province (183,490 cases) were collected. An interrupted time series (ITS) analysis was conducted using a generalized linear model (GLM) based on a negative binomial distribution. We evaluated the intervention effects of the vaccine policies while strictly controlling for autoregression, non-linear effects of meteorological factors, population dynamics, and the intensity of COVID-19 non-pharmaceutical interventions (NPIs). Stratified analyses by age group and geographical region were also performed. RESULTS: Following the introduction of the 1-dose MMR policy in 2008, no significant long-term downward trend in mumps incidence was observed across the province (IRR = 1.002, P = 0.773), and periodic outbreaks every 3 to 5 years persisted. Following the comprehensive implementation of the 2-dose MMR strategy in July 2020, the overall incidence exhibited a significant accelerated downward trend of 1.0% per month (IRR = 0.990, P = 0.019). Subgroup analyses revealed that the most heavily burdened 5-9 and 10-14 age groups experienced the most significant long-term declines (1.0% and 1.5% per month, respectively). Furthermore, the ≥15 years adult group, which was not directly targeted for vaccination, also showed a long-term reduction (0.9% per month), indicating a significant herd immunity effect. Additionally, the 2-dose policy successfully smoothed out regional incidence disparities, notably mitigating the compensatory outbreaks observed in Northern Jiangsu in 2019. CONCLUSION: A 1-dose MMR immunization schedule is insufficient to interrupt periodic mumps outbreaks, and the transition to a 2-dose strategy was associated with a steady long-term decline in overall mumps incidence across Jiangsu Province, providing valuable real-world evidence to support the continuation and optimization of 2-dose MMR immunization schedules.

title: Vaccination in Children with Paediatric Autoimmune and Autoinflammatory Rheumatic Diseases: Evidence on Safety, Immunogenicity and Effectiveness Across Live-Attenuated, mRNA and Recombinant Vaccines
abstract: Vaccination in children with paediatric autoimmune and autoinflammatory rheumatic diseases (pedAIIRDs) is clinically important but challenging. These children have an increased risk of infections due to both their underlying immune-mediated disease and the immunosuppressive therapies required for disease control. At the same time, immunosuppression may reduce vaccine-induced immune responses, while concerns about disease flares and the safety of live-attenuated vaccines may result in delayed or incomplete vaccination. This thesis aimed to generate clinically applicable, real-world evidence on the safety, immunogenicity and effectiveness of vaccination in children with pedAIIRDs receiving immunosuppressive therapy. Five studies addressed three vaccine platforms: the live-attenuated measles-mumps-rubella (MMR) booster vaccine, COVID-19 mRNA vaccines and the recombinant zoster vaccine (RZV; Shingrix). In a cohort of 186 children with juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA), MMR booster vaccination was not associated with increased disease activity, including in children receiving biological disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs, and no serious vaccine-related adverse events were observed. Long-term evaluation of 182 children with JIA showed that most patients maintained protective antibodies against measles, mumps and rubella. However, measles seroprotection five years after vaccination was significantly lower in patients receiving biologic therapy at vaccination than in those not receiving biologics, supporting a targeted approach to serological monitoring. A systematic review and meta-analysis demonstrated that COVID-19 vaccination was associated with a marked reduction in the risk of multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children (MIS-C). In a prospective cohort of 157 children with paediatric rheumatic diseases, COVID-19 mRNA vaccination induced humoral responses in nearly all patients and adequate T-cell responses in most tested patients. Although antibody concentrations were lower in patients receiving biologic therapy, vaccine effectiveness against symptomatic COVID-19 was preserved. No increase in disease activity, myocarditis or serious adverse events was identified. Finally, off-label use of RZV was evaluated in ten varicella-zoster-virus-naïve immunocompromised children for whom live-attenuated varicella vaccination was unsuitable. Nine of ten patients seroconverted following two doses. Two subsequently developed mild breakthrough varicella after household exposure and recovered without hospitalisation or antiviral treatment. Together, these studies support a shift from broad vaccine avoidance towards individualised, treatment-specific vaccination strategies in immunocompromised children. The findings provide evidence for the safe use of selected live vaccines, targeted monitoring of long-term vaccine-induced immunity, effective use of mRNA vaccines and further evaluation of non-live vaccine alternatives. These results may contribute to future national and international vaccination recommendations for children with immune-mediated inflammatory diseases.

title: Community perceptions and health-seeking behaviour towards mpox during an outbreak in Burundi: a qualitative socio-ecological analysis
abstract: Mpox remains a public health concern in Burundi and other African countries. Community knowledge, perceptions, and behaviors play an important role in disease prevention and control. This study explored perceptions of mpox, stigma and discrimination, healthcare-seeking behaviors, and other social and behavioral factors related to mpox in Burundi. A qualitative exploratory descriptive study was conducted between March and December 2025 in five provinces of Burundi as part of a multi-country study. A total of 44 purposively selected individuals participated as key informants or in-depth interviews including; recovered patients, caregivers, community members, healthcare workers, religious leaders, and traditional leaders. Data were collected through in-depth and key informant interviews using a semi-structured interview guide. Interviews were transcribed, translated into English when needed, and analyzed thematically using NVivo 14 software. Most participants had heard about mpox and recognized it as a contagious disease. However, misconceptions were common, with some people confusing mpox with measles or believing that it came only from monkeys or supernatural causes. Community health workers, health facilities, local leaders, places of worship, and radio programs were important sources of information. Some participants reported delays in seeking healthcare because symptoms were not recognized early, traditional remedies were used first, or fear of stigma discouraged timely care. Participants also described experiences of stigma and social exclusion, which sometimes affected healthcare-seeking behavior. The findings suggest that mpox prevention and control in Burundi are influenced by community knowledge, beliefs, and social experiences. Improving public awareness through trusted community actors, reducing stigma, and encouraging early healthcare seeking may strengthen efforts to prevent and control mpox outbreaks.

title: NAEGLERIA FOWLERI IS EATING BRAINS OF OUR PEOPLE: ARE WE AWARE OF THAT?
abstract: Public health is an interesting field of science in which we face challenges every day.On one hand, we are concerned with common communicable diseases like influenza, measles, chicken pox, malaria, where we have been able to protect our people with reasonable success, however, number of emerging diseases like dengue, COVID-19 and now Naegleria Fowleri infection is diverting our attention and resources.These emerging infections not only indicate a change in disease agents and host immunity but also reflect the climate change, which in turn is transforming the ecological settings where disease agents live.Man has manipulated nature for his sustenance in the name of development and at the expense of habitat of other living organisms.In doing so, he has exposed himself to certain dangers to his health and well-being.Even behaviors that are adopted for recreation has put him at risk of contracting unusual infections such as Naegleria Fowleri (brain-eating amoeba).Naegleria Fowleri is a free-living amoeba found in warm freshwater environments worldwide.It is a rare but highly lethal pathogen that can cause a devastating brain infection known as primary 1 2

full_text: AbstractTo understand the nature of the current measles outbreaks taking place across the United States in 2026, we analyzed historical surveillance data dating back to 1997 using four distinct forecasting models. By withholding data from the first four months of 2026 for out-of-sample validation, we evaluated how well traditional trend tracking and temporal dependence could anticipate this year's trajectory. While models incorporating short-term patterns performed best overall, every single model underestimated the cumulative cases recorded by May 1, 2026. This systematic underprediction reveals that the ongoing resurgence cannot be explained merely as a continuation of past trends or 2025 outbreak effects. Instead, 2026 represents a distinct, more severe outbreak regime, as the projected annual burden was already reached by May. These findings indicate that public health tracking must adapt to this heightened risk environment, and warn that the final 2026 case burden will substantially exceed that of previous years.Keywords: ARIMAX, measles, negative binomial regression, outbreak prediction, poisson regression, public health, time series analysis 2.Materials and methods2.1.Data and time indexingThe annual case series is first sorted by count year and then transformed into cumulative cases. Although the cumulative series is computed from the full available annual record, the forecasting models are trained on observations beginning in the 1996 reporting year. The 2026 observation is held out and forecasted separately. The cumulative value for count year y is plotted at January 1 of year (y+1). Therefore, a point shown at January 1, 2020 corresponds to the cumulative total through the 2019 count year. This indexing convention is used only for visualization and reporting. All covariates are defined using the original epidemiological count year. For example, the 2019 outbreak indicator is activated according to y≥2019, even though the cumulative value including 2019 cases is displayed at January 1, 2020.2.1.1.Data and extractionFigure 1 illustrates the end-to-end workflow for processing, modeling, and forecasting cumulative measles cases in the United States. The process begins with data collection, where annual cumulative measles surveillance records are obtained from publicly available sources (16) and organized into a structured time-series dataset. The collected data then undergo preprocessing, including the identification and treatment of missing observations, removal of duplicate records, correction of inconsistencies, and verification of cumulative consistency across years. The 2026 validation dataset consists of cumulative measles cases reported through May 1, 2026, obtained from the CDC Measles Cases and Outbreaks surveillance data [accessed via the Beacon reporting platform (17)]. Because these surveillance data are continuously updated as case investigations are completed, the reported cumulative total should be regarded as provisional rather than final. Consequently, the out-of-sample validation presented in this study is based on the best available surveillance data at the time of analysis, and minor revisions to the reported case counts may occur in subsequent CDC updates. However, such revisions are not expected to materially affect the qualitative conclusions regarding the comparative forecasting performance of the models. Following preprocessing, the cleaned dataset is used for model development and evaluation. Multiple forecasting approaches are fitted to the historical cumulative measles series, including Poisson generalized linear models (GLMs), quasi-Poisson GLMs, negative binomial GLMs, and an ARIMAX grid-search model. The count-regression models incorporate outbreak-related covariates to capture persistent shifts in cumulative disease burden, while the ARIMAX grid-search model combines outbreak indicators with temporal dependence. Model performance is evaluated using in-sample forecasting metrics, including the mean squared error (MSE) and root mean squared error (RMSE), together with an out-of-sample validation exercise in which the 2026 observation is withheld from model fitting and used as a holdout forecast target. To provide broader evidence of short-term forecast performance, the models are also evaluated using rolling one-year-ahead validation over the 2016–2025 test period.Figure 1Workflow for data collection, preprocessing, model development, validation, and forecasting of cumulative U.S. measles cases. Model performance is assessed using MSE, RMSE, the held-out 2026 comparison, and rolling one-year-ahead validation over the 2016–2025 test period before generating forecasts and prediction intervals.Flowchart illustrating steps for forecasting U.S. cumulative measles cases using Poisson and AutoARIMAX models: data collection, preprocessing, model development with evaluation, and forecasting future cases with prediction intervals.The final stage of the workflow consists of forecasting future cumulative measles burden using the best-performing model. Forecasts are accompanied by 95% prediction intervals to quantify uncertainty and provide insight into the potential range of future disease burden. This framework enables systematic comparison of alternative forecasting approaches and supports epidemiological surveillance, outbreak monitoring, and evidence-based public health decision-making.2.1.2.Rationale for model selectionThe forecasting models considered in this study were selected for both methodological and practical reasons. First, all four frameworks provide formal uncertainty quantification through confidence intervals or prediction intervals, which is essential for public-health decision making where uncertainty must be explicitly communicated. Reliable uncertainty estimates enable policymakers and public-health agencies to assess potential risks and prepare for a range of outbreak scenarios rather than relying solely on point forecasts. Second, the selected methods are well-suited to annual surveillance datasets such as the one analyzed in this study. Because annual measles surveillance data contain a relatively small number of observations, highly parameterized machine-learning approaches may be difficult to estimate reliably and may suffer from overfitting. In contrast, the selected statistical models can be estimated efficiently while maintaining interpretability and statistical rigor. Third, the models represent complementary forecasting philosophies. The Poisson, quasi-Poisson, and negative binomial models emphasize count-data characteristics and the estimation of outbreak-related effects, providing interpretable measures of how major resurgence periods influence cumulative disease burden. The ARIMAX grid-search model, on the other hand, focuses on exploiting temporal dependence and recent observations to improve predictive performance. Comparing these approaches, therefore, provides insight into the relative importance of outbreak-related covariates and serial dependence in forecasting cumulative measles burden. Lastly, the selected models have been widely applied in epidemiology, public health surveillance, and infectious disease forecasting. Their established theoretical foundations, interpretability, and ability to generate uncertainty estimates make them attractive tools for disease surveillance applications. By comparing these frameworks within a common forecasting setting, this study provides a practical assessment of their suitability for forecasting cumulative measles burden in the post-elimination United States.2.2.Model analytical methods2.2.1.Count-regression model formulationWe fit three generalized count-regression models to the cumulative outcome Yy: Poisson, quasi-Poisson, and negative binomial. All three models use the same log-linear mean structure,E(Yy)=λy,log⁡(λy)=ηy,whereηy=α+γtimeTy+γ2014O2014,y+γ2019O2019,y+γ2025O2025,y.Equivalently,λy=exp⁡(α+γtimeTy+γ2014O2014,y+γ2019O2019,y+γ2025O2025,y).Here,Ty=y−1996is the baseline cumulative time trend. The outbreak indicators are cumulative level-shift indicators:O2014,y={1,y≥2014,0,y<2014,O2019,y={1,y≥2019,0,y<2019,andO2025,y={1,y≥2025,0,y<2025.These variables do not represent one-year outbreak pulses. Instead, they reflect the fact that once cases occur during an outbreak year, they remain part of the cumulative total in all later observations. The 2019 indicator is motivated by the large 2019 U.S. measles resurgence, during which CDC reported the highest annual case count since 1992 (9). The 2025 indicator is motivated by the large outbreak activity reported by CDC in 2025, including outbreak-associated cases in New Mexico, Oklahoma, and Texas (10, 16).The three count-regression models differ only in their variance assumptions. The Poisson model assumesYy∼Poisson(λy),Var(Yy)=λy.The quasi-Poisson model keeps the same mean structure but allows the variance to be scaled by an estimated dispersion parameter φ:Var(Yy)=φλy.When φ>1, the quasi-Poisson model allows overdispersion relative to the Poisson model. When φ<1, it indicates underdispersion relative to the Poisson variance assumption.The negative binomial model also keeps the same log-linear mean structure but uses a quadratic mean-variance relationship:Yy∼Negative Binomial(λy,κ),Var(Yy)=λy+κλy2,where κ is the negative binomial dispersion parameter. When κ is close to zero, the negative binomial model approaches the Poisson variance structure.Additional covariates were considered during model development. A post-elimination indicator was excluded from the final count-regression specification because the training set begins in 1996, leaving only a small number of observations before the 2,000 elimination milestone. A COVID-period indicator was also evaluated but removed because it was not statistically distinguishable from zero once the baseline time trend and outbreak shifts were included.2.2.2.ARIMAX grid-search pipeline and model definitionAs a fourth forecasting approach, we fit a ARIMAX model with external regressors. In response to reviewer concerns about the previous AutoARIMAX specification, we no longer combine first differencing with permanent post-outbreak level-shift indicators. Instead, annual measles counts are modeled on the log⁡(1+Cy) scale using d=0, an explicit linear time trend, and a one-year outbreak pulse indicator. This follows the ARIMA modeling framework for time series with external regressors (12–14, 18).The data-processing pipeline for constructing the cumulative case series and assigning plotting dates is the same as for the count-regression models. Annual cases are sorted by count year, cumulative cases are computed for reporting purposes, and the plotting date is assigned as January 1 of the following year. For count year 2026, the observed partial-year cumulative value is indexed at May 1, 2026. The ARIMAX grid-search model is trained on count years 1996–2025, and the 2026 full-year cumulative forecast is displayed at December 31, 2026.Let Cy denote annual measles cases in count year y. The modeled response isZy=log⁡(1+Cy).The ARIMAX model combines a regression mean with an autoregressive error process. Specifically,Zy=β1timey+β2major_outbreaky+uy,where uy is the serially correlated regression error,timey=y−1996,andmajor_outbreaky=1{y∈{2014,2025}}.The outbreak term is therefore a one-year pulse indicator, not a permanent post-outbreak level shift, which addresses the redundancy between differencing and level-shift indicators identified in the previous specification. Although the count-regression models use a separate 2019 outbreak-shift indicator, adding a distinct 2019 pulse to the ARIMAX specification led to parameter-identifiability problems: with only annual observations and a short series, the additional pulse was weakly identified and highly collinear with the autoregressive dynamics and the estimated time trend, producing unstable coefficients and inflated standard errors. Cumulative measles cases form a smooth, monotonically increasing trajectory in which each annual value differs from the previous one by a comparatively small increment. Consequently, the observed year-to-year variability is far smaller than the variability implied by a Poisson distribution whose variance equals its large cumulative mean, driving the estimated dispersion below one. This underdispersion is therefore a structural consequence of modeling cumulative rather than incident counts.Table 3 reports the negative binomial parameter estimates.
